arxiv-1903-04646.title: An Open-Source 7-Axis, Robotic Platform to Enable Dexterous Procedures within CT Scanners
arxiv-1903-04646.creator: Dimitri A. Schreiber, Daniel B. Shak, Alexander M. Norbash, Michael C. Yip
arxiv-1903-04646.description: Abstract This paper describes the design, manufacture, and performance of a highly dexterous, low-profile, 7 Degree-of-Freedom (DoF) robotic arm for CT-guided percutaneous needle biopsy. Direct CT guidance allows physicians to localize tumours quickly; however, needle insertion is still performed by hand.

arxiv-2105-04582.title: Identifying the Quantum Properties of Hadronic Resonances using Machine Learning
arxiv-2105-04582.creator: Jakub Filipek, Shih-Chieh Hsu, John Kruper, Kirtimaan Mohan, and Benjamin Nachman
arxiv-2105-04582.description: Abstract With the great promise of deep learning, discoveries of new particles at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) may be imminent. Following the discovery of a new Beyond the Standard model particle in an all-hadronic channel, deep learning can also be used to identify its quantum numbers.

arxiv-2107-13742.title: Profile to Frontal Face Recognition in the Wild Using Coupled Conditional GAN
arxiv-2107-13742.creator: Fariborz Taherkhani*, Veeru Talreja*
arxiv-2107-13742.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Fariborz Taherkhani*, Veeru Talreja*. In recent years, with the advent of deep-learning, face recognition has achieved exceptional success. However, many of these deep face recognition models perform much better in handling frontal faces compared to profile faces. The major reason for poor performance in handling of profile faces is that it is inherently difficult to learn pose-invariant deep representations that are useful for profile face recognition.

arxiv-2109-15135.title: A Simple Sign-Bit Probabilistic Shaping Scheme
arxiv-2109-15135.creator: Vincent Corlay, Nicolas Gresset
arxiv-2109-15135.description: Abstract We propose a new shaping scheme for the Gaussian channel whose complexity is approximately half the one of a binary distribution matcher (DM). The result is obtained as follows: We first show that most of the shaping gain can be obtained via a simplified version of sign-bit shaping, which uses only two non-uniform binary sources.

arxiv-2209-12090.title: Extension of HOPS Out to 500 ParSecs (eHOPS). I. Identification and Modeling of Protostars in the Aquila Molecular Clouds HOPS: Herschel Orion Protostar Survey
arxiv-2209-12090.creator: Riwaj Pokhrel, S. Thomas Megeath, Robert A. Gutermuth, Elise Furlan, William J. Fischer, Samuel Federman, John J. Tobin, Amelia M. Stutz, Lee Hartmann, Mayra Osorio, Dan M. Watson, Thomas Stanke, P. Manoj, Mayank Narang, Prabhani Atnagulov, Nolan Habel, Wafa Zakri
arxiv-2209-12090.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Riwaj Pokhrel, S. Thomas Megeath, Robert A. Gutermuth, Elise Furlan, William J. Fischer, Samuel Federman, John J. Tobin, Amelia M. Stutz, Lee Hartmann, Mayra Osorio, Dan M. Watson, Thomas Stanke, P. Manoj, Mayank Narang, Prabhani Atnagulov, Nolan Habel, Wafa Zakri. We present a Spitzer/Herschel focused survey of the Aquila molecular clouds ( d ∼ 436 d\sim 436 pc) as part of the eHOPS (extension of HOPS Out to 500 ParSecs) census of nearby protostars.

arxiv-2210-12153.title: On amortizing convex conjugates for optimal transport
arxiv-2210-12153.creator: Brandon Amos
arxiv-2210-12153.description: Abstract This paper focuses on computing the convex conjugate operation that arises when solving Euclidean Wasserstein-2 optimal transport problems. This conjugation, which is also referred to as the Legendre-Fenchel conjugate or c c -transform, is considered difficult to compute and in practice, Wasserstein-2 methods are limited by not being able to exactly conjugate the dual potentials in continuous space.

arxiv-2405-02390.title: Towards a classification of mixed-state topological orders in two dimensions
arxiv-2405-02390.creator: Tyler D. Ellison, Meng Cheng
arxiv-2405-02390.description: Abstract The classification and characterization of topological phases of matter is well understood for ground states of gapped Hamiltonians that are well isolated from the environment. However, decoherence due to interactions with the environment is inevitable – thus motivating the investigation of topological orders in the context of mixed states.

arxiv-2411-01312.title: From Federated Learning to Quantum Federated Learning for Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks
arxiv-2411-01312.creator: Vu Khanh Quy 1 , Nguyen Minh Quy 1 , Tran Thi Hoai 2 , Shaba Shaon 3 , Md Raihan Uddin 3 , Tien Nguyen 5 , Dinh C. Nguyen 3 , Aryan Kaushik 6 , Periklis Chatzimisios 7
arxiv-2411-01312.description: Abstract 6G wireless networks are expected to provide seamless and data-based connections that cover space-air-ground and underwater networks. As a core partition of future 6G networks, Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks (SAGIN) have been envisioned to provide countless real-time intelligent applications. To realize this, promoting AI techniques into SAGIN is an inevitable trend.

arxiv-2507-02713.title: UniMC : Taming Diffusion Transformer for Uni fied Keypoint-Guided M ulti- C lass Image Generation
arxiv-2507-02713.creator: Qin Guo, Ailing Zeng, Dongxu Yue, Ceyuan Yang, Yang Cao, Hanzhong Guo, Fei Shen, Wei Liu, Xihui Liu, Dan Xu
arxiv-2507-02713.description: Abstract Although significant advancements have been achieved in the progress of keypoint-guided Text-to-Image diffusion models, existing mainstream keypoint-guided models encounter challenges in controlling the generation of more general non-rigid objects beyond humans ( e.g. , animals). Moreover, it is difficult to generate multiple overlapping humans and animals based on keypoint controls solely.

arxiv-2510-14615.title: Accelerated Multi-Modal Motion Planning Using Context-Conditioned Diffusion Models Thanks: This paper has been submitted and has not yet been peer reviewed or accepted for publication.
arxiv-2510-14615.creator: Edward Sandra, Lander Vanroye, Dries Dirckx, Ruben Cartuyvels, Jan Swevers, Wilm Decré
arxiv-2510-14615.description: Abstract Classical methods in robot motion planning, such as sampling-based and optimization-based methods, often struggle with scalability towards higher-dimensional state spaces and complex environments. Diffusion models, known for their capability to learn complex, high-dimensional and multi-modal data distributions, provide a promising alternative when applied to motion planning problems and have already shown interesting results.

arxiv-2601-22196.title: Linux Kernel Recency Matters, CVE Severity Doesn’t, and History Fades Conference: 23rd International Conference on Mining Software Repositories; April 13–14, 2026; Rio de Janeiro, Brazil 23rd International Conference on Mining Software Repositories (MSR ’26), April 13–14, 2026, Rio de Janeiro, Brazi
arxiv-2601-22196.creator: Piotr Przymus, Witold Weiner, Krzysztof Rykaczewski, Gunnar Kudrjavets
arxiv-2601-22196.description: Abstract . In 2024, the Linux kernel became its own Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) Numbering Authority (CNA), formalizing how kernel vulnerabilities are identified and tracked. We analyze the anatomy and dynamics of kernel CVEs using metadata, associated commits, and patch latency to understand what drives patching.

pmc-11536206.title: Differential effects of lifetime stressors on major depressive disorder severity: a longitudinal community-based cohort study
pmc-11536206.creator: Yingying Su, Muzi Li, Jean Caron, Daqi Li, Xiangfei Meng
pmc-11536206.description: BackgroundStressors across the lifespan are associated with the onset of major depressive disorder (MDD) and increased severity of depressive symptoms. However, it is unclear how lifetime stressors are related to specific MDD subtypes. The present study aims to examine the relationships between MDD subtypes and stressors experienced across the lifespan while considering potential confounders.

pmc-11640831.title: Health Resort Treatment Improves Functioning and Physical Performance in Long COVID Patients: A Retrospective Study
pmc-11640831.creator: Grzegorz Onik, Katarzyna Knapik, Magdalena Dąbrowska-Galas, Karolina Sieroń, Alessia Verduri
pmc-11640831.description: Background/Objectives: The physical performance and functional status of individuals with long COVID may be altered. Health resort treatment comprises balneology, exercises, physical medicine modalities, and climate therapy. Complex treatment in a sanatorium may have a positive effect on long COVID patients.

pmc-12415797.title: Antibiotic awareness: exploring knowledge among culturally and linguistically diverse patients
pmc-12415797.creator: Kylie Tran, Vinushan Kuganathan, Jessica Lam, Aqsa Rana, Serine Yau, Katherine Lee, Ravindra Dotel, Chin-Yen Yeo, Ronald L. Castelino
pmc-12415797.description: Background:Effective antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) programs must address the needs of culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) patients who often experience language barriers and varying cultural beliefs regarding antibiotics. They are at greater risk of receiving suboptimal or inappropriate care, yet guidance to support AMS practices for this population remains limited.Aim:To investigate antibiotic knowledge, perspectives, and experiences of CALD patients.

pmc-12472570.description: In industrial processes, catalysts—materials that speed up chemical reactions without being consumed—are essential. The goal of this research was to create two new rhenium-based nanocomposite catalysts that can effectively and sustainably reduce nitroaromatic compounds to aromatic amines in continuous-flow systems.

pmc-12641813.title: Ecological and Human Health Risks from Potentially Toxic Elements in Environmental Matrices of Kiteezi Landfill, Uganda
pmc-12641813.creator: Emmanuel Ebbu, Irene Nalumansi, Ivan Kiganda, Caroline Kiwanuka Nakiguli, Patrick Onen, Simon Ocakacon, Christopher Adaku, Timothy Omara, Emmanuel Ntambi, Valerio Matozzo
pmc-12641813.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). By the time of this study, Kiteezi landfill was Uganda’s largest waste disposal site and received substantial volumes of municipal solid waste. In the present study, water (n = 36), leachates (n = 36), superficial sediments (n = 30), and Colocasia esculenta corms (n = 6) were sampled from Kiteezi landfill in the dry and wet seasons of 2022 before its tragic collapse in 2024.

pmc-12646939.title: Targeting c-Jun orchestrates heat stroke-induced myocardial injury and reveals its biomarker potential
pmc-12646939.creator: Yunfei Xiang, Rui Huang, Xuemei Jiang, Qingsong Chen, Can Luo, Hongxia Wang, Junyu Jiang, Jia Xie, Guangbin Huang, Menglong Liu, Yu Ma, Dingyuan Du, Fating Zhou
pmc-12646939.description: BackgroundPatients affected by heat stroke (HS) develop myocardial injury at an early stage and exhibit a significantly higher risk of death than those without myocardial injury.MethodsWe used WGCNA and myocardial tissue transcriptome sequencing to identify candidate DEGs associated with HS-induced myocardial injury.

pmc-13215149.title: Effectiveness of the Bidimensional Bracket System in Miniscrew-Supported en Masse Retraction of the Maxillary Anterior Teeth: A Preliminary Clinical Report
pmc-13215149.creator: Abdulmalek M.H. Almasri, Mohammad Y. Hajeer, Ahmad S. Burhan
pmc-13215149.description: IntroductionIn adult Class II Division 1 cases treated by orthodontic camouflage, the extraction of the maxillary first premolars is commonly followed by retraction of the anterior segment. Achieving this movement efficiently while maintaining adequate torque control remains a major clinical concern.

pmc-13218263.title: Integrated diagnostic approach for Leptospira spp. detection in SMEDI associated reproductive disease of swine
pmc-13218263.creator: Matthias Eddicks, Annika Seifert, Julia Gründl, Katrin Strutzberg-Minder, Lina Eddicks, Robert Tabeling, Mathias Ritzmann
pmc-13218263.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Leptospirosis is a notifiable disease in human and all mammals in Germany. Besides late term abortions, leptospiral infection of sows is also mentioned as a differential in terms of SMEDI. The objective of the present study was to apply an integrated diagnostic approach in such cases under field conditions and to evaluate best suited specimen for molecular detection of Leptospira spp.

pmc-13241360.title: Prevalence and treatment of mitochondrial diabetes in Southwest Finland
pmc-13241360.creator: Nelli Rindell, Heidi Immonen, Mika H. Martikainen
pmc-13241360.description: PurposeDiabetes mellitus (DM) is a common manifestation of mitochondrial disease, typically associated with the mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) variant m.3243A>G. We investigated the clinical features, treatment, and epidemiology of mitochondrial DM in the region of Southwest Finland.MethodsElectronic medical records at Turku University Hospital were searched for patients assigned ICD-10 codes E13.0–E13.9 during 2000–2022.

pmc-13417013.title: A GPU-Oriented Onboard Imaging Framework for High-Resolution Sliding Spotlight SAR on an Embedded GPU Platform
pmc-13417013.creator: Ziyang Dai, Jian Liu, Zhanyang Ai, Yang Liu, Ziyan Wang, Zongwei Zhu
pmc-13417013.description: In conventional spaceborne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) systems, raw echo data are usually downlinked to ground stations for image formation, resulting in substantial communication burden and processing delay. Although onboard SAR imaging can alleviate this problem, onboard processors are constrained by power consumption, memory capacity, thermal dissipation, and physical size.

pmc-13571663.title: N-propargylputrescine as a minimal-tag probe for imaging putrescine dynamics in cellular homeostasis and stress
pmc-13571663.creator: Aleksandra Owczarek, Aleksandra Duchnowska, Zuzanna Sas, Maciej Zakrzewski, Anita Florkowska, Martyna Nalepa, Aleksandra Skweres, Filip Suchożebski, Alicja Mąka, Jakub Szymanowski, Piotr Michaluk, Katarzyna Winiarska, Maciej Cieśla, Anna Marusiak, Remigiusz A. Serwa, Michał Węgrzynowicz
pmc-13571663.description: SummaryPolyamines regulate multiple cellular pathways, and their intracellular availability is controlled in part by transport. We developed imaging putrescine (iPUT), a clickable putrescine analog expected to retain key properties of native putrescine and enable bio-orthogonal fluorophore conjugation for high-resolution imaging. In MCF-7 cells, iPUT accumulated predominantly in nuclei, unlike the directly fluorophore-conjugated probe BODIPY-PUT, highlighting the value of minimal tagging.
